items.title: Daryn Roongrawewan doesn't design logos, she crafts "ornamental icons"
items.summary: A profile of Berlin designer Daryn Roongrawewan, who builds brand marks she calls "ornamental icons" — like a florist's "L" that rotates into drawings of flowers — drawing her letterforms from nature and historical sources (Slavic alphabets, Victorian type, 1920s children's books) rather than chasing trends.
items.why: Manik runs an icon system and cares about editorial type; her rule that every mark should carry a meaningful connection to something recognizable is a sharp counter to generic iconography and a useful lens for CueDesign's icon language and kids' product warmth.

items.title: Mousse issue 94, Winter 2026
items.summary: A close look at the typography of contemporary-art magazine Mousse's Winter 2026 issue, pairing the pre-release typeface Costumes with François Rappo's JJannon serif across covers and spreads, with embossed and outlined type treatments in a green-and-black scheme.
items.why: High-craft editorial typography in the wild — the confident display-plus-serif pairing and physical type treatment are exactly the kind of move Manik can borrow from for Cuemath's brand system and long-form editorial layouts.

items.title: Strategies to Teach Math Conceptual Understanding
items.summary: A veteran math teacher lays out seven concrete classroom strategies for teaching the "why" behind math, not just the "how" — spiral practice, high-order tasks, visual models, hands-on manipulatives, real-world links, and getting students to explain their own reasoning.
items.why: This is Cuemath's core problem stated as teaching practice — how conceptual math understanding is actually built — with usable tactics (productive struggle, self-explanation, visual entry points) that map straight onto practice-app exercise design and tutoring flows.

items.title: Inside Linear: Building with taste, craft, and focus
items.summary: An interview with Linear co-founder and CEO Karri Saarinen on running a product company where craft, taste, and focus are the competitive edge — covering how they run design reviews, why they ship opinionated defaults, and three techniques he uses to stay focused. Free to read in full.
items.why: Linear is the design-led benchmark Manik points CueDesign at; the playbook for treating taste and craft as strategy rather than polish-applied-after-the-fact is directly applicable to how he's building the design system and the combined product.
